source_units.text:
# Maternal age effects on offspring lifespan and reproduction vary within a species

**Авторы:** Liguori Alyssa, Korm Sovannarith, Profetto Alex, Richters Emily, Gribble Kristin E.

**Журнал:** bioRxiv (2023)

**DOI:** 10.1101/2023.02.27.530305


#
source_units.reason: article_metadata_header

source_units.text: # Abstract
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Across diverse taxa, offspring from older mothers have decreased lifespan and fitness.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Little is known about whether such maternal age effects vary among genotypes for a given species, however.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We compared maternal age effects among four strains of rotifers in the Brachionus plicatilis species complex.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For each strain, we measured lifespan, reproductive schedule, and lifetime reproductive output of offspring produced by young, middle-aged, and old mothers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We found unexpected variability among strains in the magnitude and direction of maternal age effects on offspring life history traits.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In one strain, offspring of young mothers lived 20% longer than offspring of old mothers, whereas there were no significant effects of maternal age on lifespan for the other strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Across strains, advanced maternal age had positive effects, negative effects, or no effect on lifetime reproductive output.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For all but one strain, older mothers produced offspring that had higher maximum daily reproduction early in life.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Maternal age effects appear to be genetically determined traits, not features of life history strategy or due to accumulation of age-related damage in the germline.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Investigating intraspecific variability is critical for understanding the ubiquity of maternal age effects and their role in the evolution of life history and aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
## Introduction

Maternal age effects, in which a mother’s age at the time of reproduction influences the phenotype of her offspring absent of any changes in genotype, are a common form of intergenerational plasticity.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In many taxa, offspring from older mothers have decreased lifespan, fecundity, and health [1–6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As one of the earliest experimental studies of maternal age effects was conducted by Albert Lansing using the rotifer Philodina citrina [3,7], a decrease in lifespan and fecundity in old-mother offspring is often referred to as a “Lansing Effect.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ” In other species, however, advanced maternal age has positive effects [8–10] or no effects [11] on offspring fitness.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While many studies have described maternal age effects, it is unclear how they are distributed across species and whether the tendency to have positive, neutral, or negative maternal age effects is clade-specific.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A recent meta-analysis of 97 animal species has shown that Lepidopterans, other invertebrates (including C. elegans, rotifers, copepods, annelids, snails, and fruit flies), wild (non-agricultural) mammals, and humans exhibited significant negative effects of advanced maternal age, whereas wild birds had positive maternal age effects on the early development of offspring [12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The causes of maternal age effects are not clear, but are frequently thought to involve age-related shifts in trade-offs between lifespan and reproduction.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: If more resources are allocated to higher reproduction, then fewer resources can be allocated to somatic maintenance, repair, and growth, which could result in decreased lifespan, or vice versa [13–16].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, if offspring from older mothers receive fewer maternally-provisioned lipids, gene transcripts, organelles, metabolites, or other resources, they may be shorter-lived or have altered developmental and reproductive schedules.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Changes in early life reproductive schedule are thought to impact late-life reproduction or schedule and lifespan [14,17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Negative maternal age effects are hypothesized to be caused by age-related declines in the reproductive system or gamete quality, or by other physiological constraints as mothers age [3,18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Positive maternal age effects could occur in organisms with life histories, morphologies, or physiologies that enable parents to allocate more resources to offspring later in life (e.g., if older parents are larger or more experienced) [10,12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both positive and negative maternal age effects could be the result of life history adaptations, such as shifting of reproductive schedules, that optimize population fitness across generations in response to environmental changes [18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, there is limited evidence to support these hypotheses.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: With the currently available studies, it is difficult to disentangle the effects of phylogeny, life history, and environment on maternal age effects among broad taxonomic groups [12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To address questions about the evolution of life history and the impact of maternal age effects on population dynamics, it will be critical to understand the evolutionary mechanisms underlying intergenerational plasticity.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A promising avenue of investigation is to characterize intraspecific variability in maternal age effects.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Analyses among species are limited by multiple confounding variables, but within species we can compare populations or strains with relatively similar genetics, morphology, life history strategies, and environments, but distinct vital rates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Studies of Daphnia [19,20], Drosophila [4,11,21,22], and other insects [23] provide examples of high variability in the magnitude and direction of parental age effects on lifespan, development, fecundity, or embryonic diapause among strains and populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To understand whether intraspecific variability in maternal age effects is typical, additional experimental studies of other clades are needed.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Monogonont rotifers are an ideal study system for investigating phenotypic plasticity across generations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: They are microscopic invertebrate animals that are abundant worldwide and play critical roles in many aquatic food webs as primary consumers and prey.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Rotifers in the Brachionus plicatilis cryptic species complex have lifespans from 1 – 4 weeks and are easily reared across multiple, age-synchronized generations in the laboratory [24,25].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Brachionus spp. are cyclical parthenogens: they reproduce asexually, but in response to environmental cues (dense populations) can switch to a sexual reproduction phase that results in the formation of resting eggs [26].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, genetic diversity of populations can be manipulated, resulting in experimental cohorts that are isogenic, inbred, or genetically diverse.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Phenotypic plasticity and maternal effects in response to inter- and intra-specific interactions, including inducible defenses and the induction of sexual reproduction, have been studied in these rotifers for decades [27,28].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Unlike many short-lived invertebrates, Brachionus females do not produce large numbers of small offspring in broods, but instead make a large reproductive investment in each offspring, producing 1–6 large neonates each day throughout the reproductive period, with a lifetime reproductive output of 20–30 offspring.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This makes it an interesting species in which to examine the conservation of maternal age effects among strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Brachionus has externally brooded embryos, direct development with no larval stages, and no parental care after neonates hatch, so we can distinguish the effects of metamorphoses and maternal care from other maternal age-related differences in maternal provisioning [24,25].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Maternal age effects are just beginning to be explored in Brachionus rotifers. Recent studies on the Russian strain of B. manjavacas (BmanRUS), have found that advanced maternal age leads to decreased lifespan and lifetime fecundity in offspring [1,29].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While large differences in lifespan and reproductive plasticity between closely-related Brachionus strains in response to environmental stressors have been found [30,31], the variability in maternal age effects among Brachionus strains is unknown.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Here, we tested for differences in maternal age effects on offspring lifespan and reproduction among four strains from the Brachionus plicatilis species complex.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We compared one strain of B. plicatilis (BpL1) and three strains of B. manjavacas: BmanL5 and BmanRUS (both maintained in constant culture for > 20 years) and BmanRUS-RE, which was newly hatched from five-year-old resting (diapausing) eggs of BmanRUS.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We compared BmanRUS and BmanRUS-RE to test whether the life history phenotypes that have been observed in past studies were preserved in the diapausing strain (BmanRUS-RE), which had not been subjected to laboratory selective pressures for the past five years [30,31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite their genetic similarity, these strains differ in their origins, time in culture, vital rates under control laboratory conditions, and responses to environmental stressors [32,33].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Under control conditions (21°C, ad libitum food), median lifespan ranged from 10 d for BpL1 to 23.5 d for BmanL5.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: At lower temperatures (16°C), lifespans of BmanRUS and BmanL5 were extended, but the mean lifespan of BpL1 was unaffected [30].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: BmanRUS has the highest tendency for mixis (sexual reproduction), BmanL5 has less, and the BpL1 strain is completely amictic (asexual).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Under chronic caloric restriction and intermittent fasting diets, BmanRUS lifespan was significantly extended, but BmanL5 and BpL1 had no change in lifespan [31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Given the substantial differences in lifespan, reproduction, and responses to environment between these strains of the same and closely related species, we wanted to know if they also differ in the effect of maternal age on offspring phenotype.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this study, we conducted multi-generation life table experiments to quantify survivorship, lifetime reproductive output, and reproductive schedules for multiple maternal age cohorts for each strain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Since BpL1 is the most distantly related strain with the most disparate vital rates and responses to environmental conditions, we expected that it would have different maternal age effects from the other strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While BmanRUS and BmanRUS-RE are the most closely related, we hypothesized that the BmanRUS line has undergone laboratory evolution, and therefore could have distinct phenotypes from the BmanRUS-RE strain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: With these life table data, we tested for trade-offs between lifespan and reproduction and whether relationships between these factors differed among strains and maternal age cohorts.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Although previous work on BmanRUS did not find evidence for maternal age-related lifespan-reproduction trade-offs [1,29], we wanted to test whether trade-offs were lacking across the genetically distinct strains studied here.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This work will inform future research on the evolution of variability in maternal age effects within and across clades.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ## Materials & Methods
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: # Rotifer and phytoplankton culture
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Each rotifer strain was kept in serial culture and fed the chlorophyte algae Tetraselmis suecica.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Algae cultures were maintained in 2 L flasks of bubbled f/2 medium [34], minus silica, made with 15 ppt Instant Ocean Sea Salt (Instant Ocean, Blacksburg, VA) in distilled water.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both rotifer and algae cultures were grown at 21°C on a 12:12 h light:dark cycle.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Cultures of T. suecica were maintained in semi-continuous log phase growth by the removal of 40% of the culture and replacement with f/2 medium every other day throughout the experiments.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
# Life table experiments

The BmanRUS experiment took place in March 2021.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The other three strains were studied simultaneously in July 2021.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The same methods were used for all experiments.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To control for maternal and grandmaternal ages of the experimental animals, two generations of maternal age synchronization were conducted before the initiation of life table experiments.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Amictic eggs were removed from mature females by vortexing, isolated by micropipette, and allowed to hatch and mature for 5 days in ad libitum food conditions, at which time eggs were again collected from mature females.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: After repeating this for two generations, eggs were collected and allowed to hatch for 6 h to initiate the experimental cohort.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, the mothers and grandmothers of our experimental F0 cohorts were all 3 – 5 days old.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To initiate and track each cohort, individual neonates were allocated to 1 mL of T. suecica at a concentration of 6 × 105 cells mL−1 in 15 ppt Instant Ocean in 24-well plates (n = 55 to 75 per strain).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Every 24 h, each individual was observed on a Zeiss Stemi 508 microscope, scored as alive or dead, carrying or not carrying eggs (reproductive status), and the number of offspring produced within the previous 24 h was quantified.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The original female was then transferred to a new well with new seawater and T. suecica.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Daily scoring and transfers were conducted until all individuals had died.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This method produced individual-level lifespan and reproduction data.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To initiate the F1 generation at young (Y), middle (M), and old (O) maternal ages for each strain, one neonate per mother (hatched within the past 24 h) was pipetted into a well of a new plate with 1 mL of T. suecica in Instant Ocean.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In some cases, multiple neonates were taken from a single mother, particularly if other mothers had no neonates on the day of collection.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: These F1 offspring were then tracked for their entire lifetimes in the same manner as their mothers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanL5 (n = 71 – 72) and BmanRUS-RE (n = 60 – 71), experimental F1 generations were initiated at maternal ages of 3 (Y), 6 (M), and 10 d (O).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BpL1, maternal ages were 3 (n = 68), 6 (n =69), and 9 days (n =39) because of its shorter lifespan.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The F1 generation of BmanRUS had only two maternal ages: young (3 d; n = 62) and old (11 d; n = 90).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
## Statistical analyses

All data were plotted and analyzed using R v. 4.0.2 [35].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The ‘survival’ and ‘survminer’ packages [36,37] were used to create Kaplan-Meier survivorship curves.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Differences in survivorship curves among maternal age cohorts were tested within each strain using log-rank/Mantel-Haenszel tests implemented within the ‘survival’ package.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For each strain, two separate tests were used to compare Y versus M and Y versus O cohorts (except for BmanRUS, for which there was only Y and O).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The Bonferroni method was used to adjust the critical alpha value to account for multiple comparisons.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Individuals were right-censored if their death was not observed due to accidental loss during daily transfers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For lifetime reproductive output (LRO), maximum daily reproduction (MDR), age of 50% LRO, and reproductive period, differences among cohorts were tested within each strain using Kruskal-Wallis rank sum tests.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Pairwise comparisons were made using Wilcoxon rank sum tests.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To test for life history trade-offs, regression models were fit to describe the relationships between lifespan and LRO, reproductive period (in days and as a percentage of lifespan), and the age of 50% LRO.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For each strain, hypothesis tests were conducted to determine whether differences among maternal age cohorts in regression constants and coefficients were statistically significant.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: These tests were also conducted to compare strains, after pooling maternal age cohorts within each strain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
## Results

### Survivorship:

Maternal age effects on offspring lifespan differed among strains (figure 1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanL5, offspring of younger mothers (Y) lived significantly longer than offspring of older mothers (O) (median lifespans of 17 and 13.5 d, respectively; p < 0.0001).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Median lifespan of offspring of middle-aged mothers (15 d) was shorter but not significantly different than that of young-mother offspring (p = 0.128).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Offspring of younger mothers also lived longer than offspring of older mothers for BmanRUS-RE, but this difference was not significant after a Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (median lifespans of 12.5 and 11d, respectively; p = 0.047, Bonferroni corrected alpha = 0.025).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanRUS, there was no effect of maternal age on offspring lifespan (p = 0.259); median lifespan for all cohorts was 16 days.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: There was also no effect of maternal age on offspring lifespan for BpL1 (Y vs. M: p = 0.913; Y vs. O: p = 0.239).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Median lifespan for BpL1 cohorts ranged from 8–9 days, much shorter than that for the other strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Maximum lifespan (age of 5% survivorship) was similar among cohorts for BmanRUS (Y = 21 d, O = 20 d).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanL5 and BmanRUS-RE, maximum lifespan was shorter in O cohorts (BmanL5: Y and M = 22 d, O = 20 d; BmanRUS-RE: Y and M = 20 d, O = 17 d).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Maximum lifespan was shorter for BpL1 than for other strains across cohorts (Y = 15 d, M = 16 d, O = 14 d; figure 1, table S1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: ### Reproduction: Maternal age affected offspring lifetime reproductive output (LRO) in two of four strains, but these effects were in opposing directions (figure 2).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanL5, offspring of younger mothers had higher LRO (mean ± SE: 24.8 ± 0.33 neonates ind−1) than did offspring of both middle-aged and older mothers (mean ± SE: 22.1 ± 0.46 and 22.2 ± 0.49 neonates ind−1, respectively; H(3) = 57.04, p < 0.0001; figure 2G).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BpL1, LRO for all maternal age cohorts was lower than that of the other strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Offspring of young BpL1 mothers had the lowest LRO (mean ± SE: 8.5 ± 0.61 neonates ind−1), compared to older maternal age cohorts that produced just over 10 neonates individual−1 on average (H(3) = 9.33, p = 0.025; figure 2A).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For both BmanRUS and BmanRUS-RE, there was no significant effect of maternal age on offspring LRO, although offspring from older mothers tended to have higher reproductive output than offspring from younger mothers on average (BmanRUS: H(2) = 2.52, p = 0.28; BmanRUS-RE: H(3) = 8.3, p = 0.04, no significant pairwise comparisons, Wilcoxon rank sum test; figure 2C and 2E, table S1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In BmanL5, variability in LRO was twice as high in M and O cohorts than in the Y cohort (variance: Y = 7.7, M = 14.6, O = 17.2), with some M and O individuals producing very few offspring (minimum LROs of Y, M, and O cohorts, respectively: 16, 4, and 7 neonates ind−1).

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ## Reproductive period
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Reproductive period, measured as the percent of lifetime in which mothers carried eggs, was affected by maternal age in different ways among strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanL5 and BmanRUS, Y cohorts had longer reproductive periods than M (BmanL5 only) and O cohorts (BmanL5: H(3) = 32.88, p < 0.0001; BmanRUS: H(2) = 6.04, p = 0.049).

## Discussion

Maternal age effects are known to vary among species, in a manner thought to be dependent on large differences in life history strategies among evolutionarily distant taxa.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Here we show unexpected intraspecific differences in the magnitude and direction of maternal age effects on offspring lifespan and reproduction in Brachionus rotifers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Our findings suggest that maternal age effects are genetically determined traits which may differ even among closely related species with identical life history strategies.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This work implies that maternal age effects are not simply caused by the age-related accumulation of cellular or DNA damage that is passed on to offspring.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alternatively, if such damage accumulation does occur, some genotypes may have the capacity to prevent or repair resulting dysfunction in the germline.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Changes in lifespan and reproduction due to maternal age effects were not due to lifespan-reproduction trade-offs.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: BmanL5, which had the longest post-reproductive period (as a percent of the lifespan), displayed the strongest negative effects of advanced maternal age.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Median lifespan of offspring of old mothers was 20% shorter than that of offspring of young mothers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Offspring of young mothers had higher lifetime reproductive output (LRO), with lower variability among individuals, and longer reproductive periods relative to offspring of old mothers.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: BmanRUS was least affected by maternal age: both lifespan and LRO were similar between young and old mother cohorts, though advanced maternal age in BmanRUS did lead to shorter reproductive periods and the production of more neonates early in life.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BmanRUS-RE, a strain that was initiated with BmanRUS resting eggs from 2016, offspring of younger mothers had a 10% higher median lifespan (though this difference was not significant), and there was no effect of maternal age on LRO.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: BmanRUS-RE had the largest difference in early-life reproductive peaks between old and young mother cohorts across strains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For all B. manjavacas strains, old mother cohorts produced the majority of their offspring earlier in life than young mother cohorts.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For BpL1, the most distantly-related strain with the shortest lifespan and lowest reproduction overall, advanced maternal age led to higher LRO, but had no effect on lifespan.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similarly, Anderson and colleagues [20] studied multiple strains of Daphnia magna and found an “inverse Lansing Effect” in some strains, in which offspring of older mothers lived longer than offspring of younger mothers.

source_units.text: They hypothesized that this inverse effect could be a result of decreased lipid offspring provisioning by older mothers, which could result in embryonic caloric restriction.

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Maternal age effects on offspring lifespan and reproduction are genotype-specific in Brachionus rotifers. Resource trade-offs between lifespan and reproduction likely do not underlie the variable effects observed here.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: More studies examining intraspecific variability in maternal age effects are needed to determine whether such high variation is widespread among clades or specific to arthropods and rotifers (the most well-studied taxa to date).
